figures.title: State and questions in, typed answers out, code routes
figures.desc: The state and the fixed question set go to the model. The model returns only typed answers. Code validates them and draws the routes.
figures.caption: The model answers fixed questions; software owns everything that happens next.
figures.transcript: Flow of four steps: build the state from the case; ask seven typed questions per message; receive typed answers only; validate, measure, and route in code.

items.label: Ask typed questions
items.detail: seven per message, fixed answer sets

items.label: Receive typed answers
items.detail: a probability, a choice, or a level

items.label: Validate, measure, route
items.detail: code and people, not the model

figures.title: Label the sample, freeze it, run, then compare
figures.desc: Your labels for ten messages are written and frozen before the model runs. The comparison afterwards is the only evidence about the answers.
figures.caption: Labels first, run second, comparison third.
figures.transcript: Timeline of four steps: label ten messages yourself; freeze the labels with a digest and time; run the decision function once; compare its answers with your labels.

figures.title: Declared confidence is a claim; measured agreement is evidence
figures.desc: The model's declared confidence is a number it writes about itself. Agreement with frozen labels is measured. A gate is set from the measurement.
figures.caption: Set gates from what you measured, not from what the model declared.
figures.transcript: Comparison of four items: declared confidence comes from the model; measured agreement comes from frozen labels; a wrong answer with high declared confidence means the number did not protect you; a gate is set above the highest confidence any wrong answer carried.

items.label: Wrong but confident
items.detail: the number did not protect you

figures.title: Routes drawn from typed answers and gates, in order
figures.desc: Supersession first, then the instruction gate, then the request gate, then usable size and quantity, then authority, then declared confidence. Only a message that passes every gate is picked.
figures.caption: A message is picked only after every earlier rule lets it through.
figures.transcript: Stack of six rules in order: replaced by a later message is superseded; instructs the desk is referred; not a request is ignored; mixed sizes or no usable quantity is reviewed or clarified; no authority is referred; weak declared confidence is reviewed; what remains is picked.

items.label: Tells the desk what to do
